newsitem.title: USA: Man who tipped police to Cunanan may miss reward.
newsitem.headline: Man who tipped police to Cunanan may miss reward.

text.p: Fernando Carreira, the houseboat caretaker whose telephone call led police to Andrew Cunanan, may not be eligible for the $45,000 reward promised for the arrest of the suspected serial killer, police said on Thursday.

Miami Beach Police Chief Richard Barreto told a news conference the caretaker's actions did not seem to correspond to terms of various rewards offered for catching whoever was responsible for the July 15 slaying of Gianni Versace.
Police believe Cunanan shot the famous fashion designer dead with the same gun he used to kill himself on board the houseboat on Wednesday night.
"It is not my understanding that the caretaker provided information specifically with the intent of telling us where Mr. Cunanan was," he said.
Under the terms of the FBI's reward offer, the money would go to anyone who provided "information leading to the apprehension of Cunanan."
Carreira was going to check on the houseboat on Wednesday afternoon, when he saw that a door was ajar. He went inside and that some articles had been moved, alerting him that someone was inside.
He then heard a shot, and left the houseboat to use his cellular telephone to call police. But in the meantime, he kept watch on the door to make sure that no one left, Barreto said.
Police declined comment on whether the Carreira was suspected of harbouring Cunanan, or whether they thought Cunanan had been holed up in the houseboat for days after Versace's death.
Barreto said a decision on the reward money, which has been offered by groups including the FBI and various Miami and Florida law enforcement agencies, would be forthcoming.
"I will have a great deal to do with that decision, but I will make it in concert with other officials," Barreto said.
